content.comment_body: Can anyone clarify the following? In the PI Controller function block, there's a SP (setpoint) value and a button labeled 'reference' beside it. What is the purpose of this? Is it possible to have the same SP variable (changed manually via text input) in two different PI controllers? Also, is the analog marker a flag or an actual value stored in memory?

Hello! The 'reference' feature allows you to use the value from an existing analog block as a parameter for the current block. You can indeed use the same value in multiple blocks by utilizing 'reference.' Just assign the desired value as SP in the output of an analog block, then set this block as the reference in the PI Controller. Hope this clarifies things!

analysis.insight_summary: The user is unsure about the function of the 'reference' button in the PI Controller and whether a single setpoint value can be used across different instances. The community clarifies that the reference option enables an existing analog block's output to serve as a shared parameter (SP) for multiple controllers, enhancing both configuration flexibility and component reuse.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects clearer documentation or interface guidance on how the 'reference' function in the PI block works, as well as confirmation that setpoint values can be effectively reused among various controller blocks.
